kinds.d: Rechargeable or battery toothbrush whose head oscillates, rotates or vibrates to clean the teeth.
Replacement brush head for an electric toothbrush; the one spare-parts entry for powered brushes.
Toothbrush with a fixed head and no motor; baby and training brushes are included.
Paste or gel used with a toothbrush to clean the teeth, usually containing fluoride.

kinds.a: floss · dental tape · floss pick · interproximal brush
kinds.d: Thread, tape or small brush for cleaning between the teeth where a toothbrush cannot reach.
Liquid rinsed around the mouth to reduce plaque, freshen breath or deliver fluoride.
Powered device that cleans between teeth with a pulsed jet of water.

brands.d: Procter & Gamble oral-care brand of manual and electric toothbrushes, heads, floss and toothpaste; launched in California in 1950.
eras: Gillette group from 1984; Braun electric brushes sold as Oral-B
Procter & Gamble after the 2005 Gillette acquisition

brands.d: Philips brand of sonic electric toothbrushes and flossers, first launched in 1992 by GEMTech/Optiva of Washington state.
Fort Collins, Colorado maker of oral irrigators, begun in 1962 as Aqua Tec; now part of Church & Dwight.
Colgate-Palmolive oral-care brand of toothpastes, toothbrushes, mouthwash and floss, sold since 1873.
Procter & Gamble toothpaste brand, sold as Blend-a-med in much of Europe.
Haleon brand of toothpaste and mouthwash for sensitive teeth; sold as Shumitect in Japan.
Haleon brand of toothpaste and mouthwash aimed at bleeding gums and gum disease.
Toothpaste brand of GABA of Therwil, first to use amine fluoride; owned by Colgate-Palmolive since 2004.
Oral-care brand of Swiss company Curaden, known for ultra-soft manual toothbrushes with Curen filaments.
Antiseptic mouthwash brand, sold over the counter since 1914 and now owned by Kenvue.
Privately held Malmö company that began with a triangular dental stick and is known for interdental brushes.
eras: Founded 1965 by wood-carver Henning Eklund with Malmö School of Dentistry

traditions.d: Cleaning the teeth with a chewed twig: the miswak of Salvadora persica in the Islamic world, neem datun in India and chew sticks across Africa.
traditions.tech: The end of a fresh twig is chewed until its fibres splay into a brush; used before prayer in Islamic practice.
traditions.mat: Salvadora persica (arak, 'toothbrush tree'); neem; banyan and other local trees
traditions.auth: True miswak is cut from Salvadora persica; other woods are sold as generic chew sticks.
